note: Client-only. The server's /api/auth/refresh already rotates single-use refresh tokens correctly; nothing under app/server changes. Previous ledger (Sprint 6) archived at .agents/docs/archive/sprint-6-feature-list.json.

features.title: authSession — single in-flight refresh coordinator
features.description: lib/authSession.ts owns token lifecycle outside React: read/write tokens, decode `exp`, and `refreshOnce()` with a module-level in-flight promise so N concurrent callers produce one POST /api/auth/refresh. AuthContext cannot be the mechanism — services are not React and cannot call a hook.
steps: Two concurrent refreshOnce() calls resolve from ONE network request (asserted by counting requests, not by inspecting code)
A successful refresh writes accessToken, refreshToken and user to localStorage before resolving
The in-flight slot is cleared on both success and failure — a failed refresh does not poison every later call with a rejected promise
isExpired() returns true for a token whose `exp` has passed and false for a live one, applying the skew
FAILURE CASE: a malformed / non-JWT token makes isExpired() return false rather than throwing — never log someone out over a parse bug
features.notes: Verified in-browser: 6 concurrent fetchWithAuth calls past expiry produced exactly ONE POST /api/auth/refresh (counted by patching window.fetch) and six 200s. isExpired() returns false for garbage, empty and null tokens.

features.title: Terminal vs. survivable refresh failure
features.description: A 401 from /refresh, or no stored refresh token, ends the session. A network failure does not — it throws to the caller with the session intact, matching the rule AuthContext's hydrate path already follows.
steps: Refresh answering 401 clears accessToken, refreshToken and user from localStorage
Refresh failing with a network error leaves all three in localStorage untouched
With no refreshToken stored, refreshOnce() rejects immediately without issuing a request
FAILURE CASE: a 500 from /refresh is treated as survivable, not terminal — the server being broken is not the user's session being over
features.notes: Verified by driving refreshOnce() against stubbed responses: 401 with an unchanged token throws SessionExpiredError and clears storage; 500 and a thrown TypeError both leave accessToken/refreshToken/user intact.

features.title: Cross-tab race — adopt the winner's token instead of logging out
features.description: Refresh tokens are single-use. Two tabs that both refresh mean one presents a deleted row and gets a 401. Before treating that 401 as terminal, re-read localStorage: if the access token changed while our refresh was in flight, another tab won — adopt its token and continue.
steps: Simulating the loss (stored access token replaced mid-flight, refresh answering 401) resolves with the NEW token instead of throwing
The session is NOT cleared in that case — localStorage still holds a user
The same 401 with an unchanged stored token IS terminal
FAILURE CASE: an unrelated 401 while the token happens to be rewritten with the SAME value is still terminal — the comparison is on value, not on a write happening
features.notes: Verified: with /refresh answering 401 while the stored access token was rewritten mid-flight, refreshOnce() resolved with the winner’s token and the session was kept. The same 401 with an unchanged token stayed terminal.

features.title: fetchWithAuth — pre-flight refresh + retry once on 401
features.description: The primary surface (services/projects.ts, team.ts, notifications.ts, sessions.ts via api/request.ts). Refresh before sending when the token is already expired; retry exactly once on a 401; skip both for the auth routes.
steps: With an expired token, one call produces a refresh and then the real request — and the real request is never sent with the dead token
A 401 from an otherwise valid request triggers one refresh and one retry, and the caller receives the retried 200
A 401 on the RETRY is returned to the caller unchanged — exactly one retry, no loop
POST /api/auth/login answering 401 (wrong password) does not trigger a refresh
FAILURE CASE: a request with a JSON body that gets retried sends the body again intact, not an empty second request
features.notes: Verified both paths separately. Pre-flight: an expired token refreshes before sending and the dead token never goes out. Reactive: a forged token with a far-future exp but a bad signature produced a real 401, one refresh, and a 200 on the retry. A wrong-password 401 from /login fired zero refreshes.

features.title: axios interceptor — same policy for the Bug Tracker
features.description: services/api.ts (logs + tickets) is a separate axios instance with its own request interceptor and no 401 handling. A response interceptor applies the identical refresh-and-retry policy, guarded by a per-config retried flag.
steps: A 401 from a tickets call refreshes once and replays the request, and the caller sees the data
The replayed request carries the NEW bearer token, not the stale one from the original config
A second 401 on the replay propagates as an axios error rather than looping
FAILURE CASE: a 403 or 500 is passed through untouched — only 401 triggers the path
features.notes: Verified: ticketsAPI.getAll() with a forged token refreshed once and returned 2 rows. The replay carries the new bearer token, set explicitly on the config.

features.title: Migrate the six raw-fetch modules onto fetchWithAuth
features.description: noteApi.ts, noteAi.ts, calendarApi.ts, chatApi.ts, useDashboardStats.ts, useNoteStatsOverview.ts each call fetch() with getAuthHeaders() and therefore get no retry. 11 call sites, mechanical. Without this, 'tokens no longer expire mid-session' would be false for Notes, Calendar, Chat and the Dashboard.
steps: grep finds no remaining `fetch(` paired with getAuthHeaders() outside api/client.ts and services/auth.ts
Notes, Calendar, Chat and Dashboard all still load normally after the swap (no behaviour change on the happy path)
With an expired token, each of those surfaces recovers instead of erroring
FAILURE CASE: a module that sent its own Content-Type still sends it — the swap must not drop request headers
features.notes: Verified: grep finds getAuthHeaders with exactly one consumer left (api/client.ts). Walking Dashboard, Bug Tracker, Chat, Projects and Notes past expiry via client-side navigation produced ONE refresh and ZERO failed requests.

features.title: AuthContext reacts to an expired session
features.description: Clearing localStorage is not enough — React still holds `user` and keeps rendering a signed-in shell. AuthContext subscribes to authSession's session-expired event and drops its state, and also listens to `storage` so a sign-out in another tab is honoured here.
steps: A terminal refresh failure flips isAuthenticated to false without a reload, and ProtectedRoute redirects to /login
The redirect carries state.from, so signing back in returns to the page the user was on
Signing out in a second tab logs this tab out too
The subscription is torn down on unmount — no listener leak across provider remounts
FAILURE CASE: a survivable (network) refresh failure does NOT log the user out of the shell
features.notes: Verified without a reload: a terminal refresh failure redirected to /login, and history.state carried from=/dashboard. Signing out in a second tab logged the first tab out too.

features.title: authApi's own calls stop hand-rolling auth headers
features.description: services/auth.ts calls getProfile/updateProfile/changePassword/updateSettings with hand-built Authorization headers, so they are the one authed surface left without retry. They move onto fetchWithAuth; login, register, refresh and logout deliberately stay on raw fetch — they are the skip-list.
steps: getProfile, updateProfile, changePassword and updateSettings recover from an expired token
login with a wrong password still surfaces the server's message and does NOT trigger a refresh
refreshToken() itself still uses raw fetch — it is what the retry path calls, and routing it through the retry would recurse
FAILURE CASE: getProfile against a genuinely dead session still throws the 401 that AuthContext's hydrate path depends on
features.notes: Verified: getProfile, updateProfile, changePassword and updateSettings now route through fetchWithAuth and recover from expiry; login/register/refresh/logout stay on raw fetch and are also skipped by path in api/client.ts.

features.title: End-to-end: a tab past token expiry keeps working
features.description: The sprint's own exit criterion, run for real against the API with a short JWT_EXPIRY so the hour does not have to be waited out.
steps: Sign in with JWT_EXPIRY set to a few seconds; wait past it; navigate the app — every surface loads, and the network log shows exactly one refresh
Load a page that fires several authed requests at once past expiry — still exactly one refresh, and every request succeeds
Revoke the refresh token server-side, then act — the app lands on /login rather than showing a broken shell
FAILURE CASE: stop the API entirely and act — the user is NOT logged out, and the error names the unreachable server
features.notes: Verified end to end with JWT_EXPIRY set to 20s then 45s (restored to 1h afterwards). Past expiry the app keeps working with one refresh. With the API stopped, an expired token and a failed refresh, the user is NOT logged out — still on /dashboard with tokens intact.
